privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What Porchlamps records, why it's needed, how long it's kept, and what you can do with your own data.
privacy.intro: Porchlamps only records the information needed to keep the site working. This page explains what we record, why we need it, how long we keep it, and what you can do with your own data.

stored.0: Your Google account identifier (sub) and the email verified by Google: stored only if you choose to sign in. The sub is used to recognize your house. The email is used for only two things: sending you email when you turn on "Tell me by email in the morning", and confirming it's you when you write to ask for your data to be deleted. The email is not made public and is not used for anything else. We don't store your name or profile picture. People who don't sign in with Google can leave an email themselves to get the morning email. It's only sent after you click the link in the confirmation email, which is also sent through Cloudflare; if you don't click it, no morning email is sent.
stored.1: Nickname: one you choose yourself, or one picked for you at random.
stored.2: The line you leave, and the city or district you chose at the time. What everyone sees is "so-and-so in some city or district".
stored.3: The lamps you light and the ones you receive. The city or district you chose and the time when you light a lamp become a small postmark, sent to the other person.
stored.5: What you write in the "Wishing well", and the optional contact info: once sent, it becomes a to-do item in the author's private GitHub project, along with your browser version information, and with your house code if you have a house. These are not stored in Porchlamps' database and are not made public.
stored.6: A hash of your IP: used to prevent abuse and to handle reports. The hashing key is changed every night, and the hash can't be turned back into the original IP.
stored.7: Notification subscriptions: stored only when you turn on notifications on your profile page or after you've said your line. It contains the push address the browser gives, the encryption keys, and which kinds of notifications you turned on. It's only used to send these three kinds of notifications: "someone lit a lamp for you", "some lamps lit up for you", and "a reminder in the evening to come back". The "someone lit a lamp for you" notification says which city or district the person lighting the lamp is in and which lamp they lit. Notifications never contain any content of a line or any nickname. Notifications are encrypted and passed along by your browser vendor's push service (for example Google, Apple, or Mozilla), which can't see the content.
stored.8: One cookie: used only to recognize who you are, so that when you come back next time you return to the same house. During the few minutes of signing in there is also a temporary cookie, which is cleared once it's been used.
stored.9: Your browser's localStorage: helps remember which small tips you've seen, how many lamps you've lit tonight, and whether you've dismissed the sign-in or "Add to Home Screen" reminders. These stay only on your own device.
stored.10: Sponsorship records: only if you sponsor through "Buy the author a coffee". We store the email you enter, the optional name and message, the amount, whether it's monthly or one-time, and the record of each charge and e-invoice (the time, whether it succeeded, and the invoice number). Your card number is entered on ECPay's payment page; Porchlamps never receives it and doesn't store it. These records have no connection to your Porchlamps account or house, and are not matched against the email you sign in with. The sponsorship email is used for only four things: charge notices, the link to manage a monthly sponsorship, e-invoices, and the author's reply to your message. It does not get the morning email.
stored.11: Your browser's time zone name (for example, Asia/Taipei): used to separate each night by the time where you are, and so that notifications and the morning email reach you in your morning and evening. Others can't see it.

privacy.purpose: This data is only used to keep Porchlamps running: recognizing your house, showing your words to others, counting the lamps on houses and the map, and blocking abuse and handling reports. It is not used for ads, is not sold, and is not given to anyone.

keep.0: Lines, lamps, and house: kept until you delete your account. Others can see your line on tonight's screen for 24 hours; if your house is open, they can also see your lines from the last 7 nights.
keep.1: IP hashes used for rate limiting: deleted after 2 days. The one attached to a report is deleted together with that line.
keep.2: Notification subscriptions: until you turn notifications off, delete your account, or the push service tells us the subscription is no longer valid.
keep.3: The cookie that recognizes you: 400 days. The temporary sign-in cookie: 10 minutes.
keep.4: Wishing well: kept in the author's private GitHub project. To have it deleted, write to the author.
keep.5: Sponsorship records: a monthly sponsorship is kept for 365 days after it's canceled or all of its payments are done; a completed one-time payment is kept for 90 days; orders that were never paid are deleted after 3 days for monthly and 8 days for one-time (ATM and convenience store payments need time to be paid). When they're deleted, their charge records are deleted with them. Records held by ECPay and for e-invoices are kept as ECPay's rules and tax law require.
keep.6: Email addresses that haven't been confirmed: kept for up to two days, then deleted.

whoSees.0: Others can see your nickname, your city or district, and your line from tonight; also your house's lines from the last 7 nights and what your house looks like (without lamp counts), and, when you light a lamp, the nickname and postmark next to the lamp. If you agree to share, others can turn a line into an image without your nickname, city or district and share it outside the site. The house part can be turned off on your profile page; for people who joined before this feature launched, the house is off by default, and lamps they lit earlier don't carry a nickname.
whoSees.1: The author can see all lines (including hidden ones), to handle reports and keep the community safe.
whoSees.2: Only the author can see what you write in the wishing well.
whoSees.3: The author can see recordings of screen activity in Microsoft Clarity. They include the lines and nicknames that were on screen at the time, but not your Google account.
whoSees.4: When someone writes something heavier, or a line is hidden because it was reported, the author gets a notification on Discord. The notification only contains a number, and does not include what the line said.
whoSees.5: Sponsors' email, name, message, and amount can be seen only by the author, and never appear anywhere on Porchlamps; lamps, houses, and the map have nothing to do with sponsorship.
whoSees.6: The author can see your time zone name on the admin page, and uses it only to fill in lamps by the time where you are on New Year's Eve.

privacy.servicesLead: Porchlamps uses the services below. They handle the data that passes through them according to their own privacy policies:

0.name: Cloudflare
0.use: Site hosting and database; data may be stored outside Taiwan, Hong Kong and Japan. It also sends the morning email, the email confirmation, and sponsorship charge notices, and only gets the recipient's email address and the contents of the email

1.name: Google sign-in
1.use: Only used when you choose to sign in. Google only sends back your sub and email

3.name: Google Analytics 4
3.use: Measures overall use. It only sends event names and counts, and does not include the content of lines or personal identity. It sets its own cookie, which you can turn off with your browser's tracking protection

4.name: Microsoft Clarity
4.use: To understand how people use the interface (clicks, scrolling, and screen recordings). Text in input boxes is masked automatically, but the lines and nicknames shown on screen are recorded. It sets its own cookie, which you can turn off with your browser's tracking protection

5.name: GitHub
5.use: Where the wishing well is stored: the author's private project, which only the author can see

6.name: Discord
6.use: Where the author receives notifications. It only receives a number

7.name: ECPay
7.use: Sponsorship payments and e-invoices. What you fill in on the payment page is handled by ECPay. The email you enter is given to ECPay to issue the e-invoice and keep it in ECPay's e-invoice carrier under that email, and ECPay sends you the notice that it was issued

privacy.rights: Under Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act, you can ask to look up, view, copy, correct, stop the use of, or delete your data. The most direct way is in "My house": it has all of your lines and lamps. From the top right you can go to your profile page to change your nickname, city or district, and to decide whether others can visit your house. "Delete account" at the very bottom clears your account, the words you've said, the lamps you've received, and your whole house together, and it can't be undone. As for the lamps you lit for others, they stay in their houses anonymously and are no longer connected to you in any way. If you're in Hong Kong, under Hong Kong's Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, you can likewise ask to access and correct your data, in the same way as above.
privacy.rightsJapan: If you live in Japan, under Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information, you can likewise ask to see your data, or to have it corrected, deleted, or no longer used, also in the same way as above. Porchlamps is looked after by one author in Taiwan. The data is mainly kept on servers run by Cloudflare, an American company, and most of the other services listed on this page are American companies too (ECPay is in Taiwan), so your data may not be kept in Japan. The United States has no single, comprehensive federal privacy law like Japan's; Porchlamps keeps only the data listed on this page and handles it as described above under "How long we keep it" and "Who sees this". The data is used only for what this page describes; apart from the services listed on this page, it isn't given to anyone, and it isn't sold.
privacy.rightsUS: If you live in the United States, including California, you can ask what data we keep about you, and ask us to correct or delete it, in the same ways as above. Using these rights won't change how you're treated here. Porchlamps does not sell your data, and does not share it with anyone for cross-site advertising.
privacy.rightsEU: If you live in the EU, the EEA or the UK, the GDPR (in the UK, the UK GDPR) lets you see, correct or delete your data, ask us to restrict or stop using it, and get a copy you can take with you, in the same ways as above. If you think we've handled your data wrongly, you can complain to the data protection authority where you live. We use your data on two bases: what Porchlamps needs in order to work (legitimate interest), and your consent for the things you turn on yourself (signing in, notifications, the morning email), which you can turn off at any time. The data is mainly kept on servers run by Cloudflare, an American company, so it is transferred outside Europe.
privacy.analyticsConsent: If you're in the EU, the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, Porchlamps asks you first before using Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity. You can change your answer on your profile page at any time.
privacy.rightsMail: For other requests, you can write to the author. If you write from the email you signed in with, the author can confirm it's you. If you write from another address, the author can only search using the nickname, city or district, and date you give in the email, and can't confirm that the sender is the owner of the house.
privacy.changes: When what we store or how it's used changes, this page and the date above will be updated.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: A few things we'd like you to know before you leave a line or light a lamp on Porchlamps.
terms.intro: Porchlamps is a place where people keep each other company at night. Before you start, please look through these points. Continuing to use it means you agree to them.
terms.who: You must be at least 13 years old to use it. If you're under 18, please let a parent or guardian know first.

dont.0: Don't leave any contact information (such as a phone number, social media account, or email).
dont.1: Don't leave personal information that could identify you or someone else.
dont.2: Don't harass, insult, or threaten others, or pretend to be someone else.
dont.3: Don't post ads or scam messages, or use programs to leave lines, light lamps, or report in bulk.

terms.words: What you say belongs to you. You agree that Porchlamps may display it in order to provide the service: shown to others for 24 hours, and afterward kept only in your house until you delete your account. Share cards don't include anyone's line unless the person who wrote it agrees that line can be shared. That agreement can be withdrawn at any time, but an image that has already been shared can't be taken back.

care.0: A line reported by two different people is hidden for now, and reviewed by the author.
care.1: The author can hide lines and restrict people who break the rules, without further notice.
care.2: This place is run by the author alone, who isn't on call at night, so a quick response can't be guaranteed.

terms.house: A house that isn't signed in is only remembered in this browser's cookie, and can't be found again once it's cleared. If you sign in with Google, you can get back to the same house even on another device. You can delete your account at any time.

sponsor.0: Sponsoring is voluntary. It doesn't get you anything in return, and it doesn't change who gets seen; lamps, houses, and the map have nothing to do with sponsorship.
sponsor.1: Payments are handled by ECPay. A monthly sponsorship charges the same amount once a month until you cancel it with the manage link in the email; after you cancel, there are no more charges.
sponsor.2: Sponsorships are generally not refunded once complete. If you were charged twice or entered the wrong amount, please write to the author within {days} days of paying, with the payment time and amount. Once confirmed, it will be refunded in full.

terms.notService: Porchlamps is not a counseling or crisis service. If you need someone to talk with, the About page has hotlines you can call.
terms.asIs: Porchlamps is provided as is, and may be interrupted, changed, or stopped. The author will do their best to preserve every house, but can't guarantee that data will never be lost. To the extent the law allows, the author is not responsible for indirect losses caused by using Porchlamps.
terms.changes: When the terms change, this page and the date above will be updated. If you keep using Porchlamps afterward, it means you agree to the new terms.
terms.law: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan). Any dispute arising from them will have the Taiwan Taipei District Court as the court of first instance.
